steps.what: Plan hydroelectric plant upgrades with technical and operational constraints
Manage hydroelectric upgrades with delivery teams and resolve operational issues

tasks.design: The manager develops the upgrade plan with technical staff and coordinates delivery through {PROJECT}. Existing documents in {DOCS} support the work without replacing plant-specific planning or issue resolution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Upgrade choices depend on equipment, operating constraints and delivery dependencies.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared project records improve access without establishing a reduction in coordination time.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing outage, reliability and delivery trade-offs.
tasks.human_edge: The manager negotiates workable decisions with the people responsible for delivery.
tasks.altitude: Upgrade leadership and decision rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate plant availability during an upgrade

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: plant upgrade planning and coordination remain human; no recurring clerical baseline is specified.

assumptions: Boundary is manager planning and coordination, not engineering design, installation labour or corporate project authorisation.

Technical staff supply existing options and operating constraints. The manager produces the plan in s1; responsible project authorities provide required authorisations after planning and before delivery in s2. Delivery teams produce progress during s2 before issue resolution; outside work is unchanged.
No free structured upgrade-feasibility flag is assumed. Check native project functions first; existing runtime earns no labour saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new automation or reporting requirement is introduced.
research_questions: Which project activities have a separately measurable clerical baseline?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+55=100; net 0%. Planning and delivery coordination retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and review hydroelectric operating documents

steps.what: Develop or review budgets, plans, contracts, rates, procedures and engineering studies

tasks.design: The manager develops and reviews the actual operating documents in {DOCS}, using financial records in {ERP} and contract versions in {CLM}. The broad task does not establish a common data-entry or first-draft baseline across these different documents.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document conclusions depend on plant, engineering and commercial context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records support substantive review; no single automated judgement covers the listed documents.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing assumptions, consequences and inconsistent technical or commercial evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The manager understands how each proposal affects plant operation.

reach.task: Coordinate operational comments on technical and commercial proposals

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: these varied documents require substantive development or review. A generic drafting or arithmetic saving cannot be inferred across the whole task.

assumptions: Boundary is manager development and review of the listed documents, excluding original engineering investigations, negotiation and final external signature.

Responsible finance, engineering and contract staff supply existing proposals and evidence. The manager checks assumptions and produces comments or revised documents within s1; no free structured technical conclusion is assumed.
Test document-specific native templates before custom drafting; existing runtime earns no labour saving. Zero incremental upkeep because this design introduces no new system.
unknowns: Actual mix of documents and repeated preparation work
research_questions: Which document type has recurring copying or drafting that can be measured separately from substantive review?

already_counted.description: Substantive development and review of operating documents

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. The scenario retains substantive work across the unspecified document mix.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and implement generation-policy evaluation procedures

steps.what: Develop policy evaluation procedures for hydroelectric generation activities

loop.purpose: Draft evaluation procedure wording after the manager defines the evaluation approach
loop.input: Manager-selected policy versions, objectives, criteria, evidence sources and decision boundaries
loop.output: Draft procedure with source notes and explicit gaps
loop.check: Manager checks that criteria test the intended policy, evidence is obtainable, limitations are explicit and escalation steps preserve decision authority
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported criteria or missing evidence return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle headings, but expressing the selected evaluation approach needs contextual wording; test native templates first

steps.what: Review and implement policy evaluation procedures with responsible plant staff

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} templates before a bounded loop drafts wording for the manager's selected evaluation approach. The manager checks the procedure's meaning, approves its exact version and implements it with plant staff through existing {OPS_SYSTEM} arrangements.
tasks.previous_blocker: Turning a selected evaluation approach into clear instructions takes drafting effort.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can reuse supplied policy evidence without choosing evaluation standards.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing meaningful criteria and handling evidence that cannot support a conclusion.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides what the evaluation should establish and how staff should act on it.
tasks.altitude: A modest reduction in wording work; evaluation and implementation authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate evidence collection for a policy evaluation
reach.learn: Evaluation design and limits of operational evidence

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: bounded procedure drafting may reduce wording time after evaluation design and source checking. No hydroelectric case establishes the proposed saving.

assumptions: Boundary is procedure development and implementation, not conducting every later evaluation or changing plant operating controls.

Within retained s1 time the manager selects policy versions and captures evaluation purpose, scope, criteria, evidence-source IDs, responsible roles, reporting fields and escalation boundaries before requesting a draft. The 51 retained hours include this design, capture and semantic correction; no free structured evaluation brief is assumed.

Existing evidence owners supply available records under unchanged processes. Missing sources or unsuitable criteria require manual procedure writing; the loop cannot invent measures or interpret compliance conclusively.

Test native procedure templates first. Existing system runtime earns no labour saving. Five extra focal hours count template changes, sampled procedure checks and failed-draft handling; no new staff data-entry demand is introduced.
unknowns: Policies covered and existing evaluation evidence
research_questions: Does drafting reduce hands-on time after criterion design, meaning checks and implementation are included?

already_counted.description: Evaluation design, input capture, drafting correction and meaning checks
Final procedure approval and staff implementation

incremental.description: Template changes, sample checks and failed-draft handling

approvals.approved_version: Exact evaluation procedure, policy versions, criteria, evidence sources, roles and escalation boundaries reviewed in s2; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=60*0.85+40=91, gross 9%, net 4% after 5 focal upkeep. Range covers failed drafts with no gain through 7 points of wording removed minus 5 upkeep. Criterion selection and implementation keep their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create and enforce hydrostation voltage schedules

steps.what: Create or enforce hydrostation voltage schedules within authorised operating requirements

tasks.design: The manager creates or enforces the schedule using existing plant-control information {OTHER} and authorised network requirements. Existing automatic voltage regulation remains unchanged and earns no new labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Schedule choices depend on network obligations and current plant conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing control displays support decisions without establishing autonomous schedule authority.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling changing network requirements and plant limits.
tasks.human_edge: The manager recognises when a proposed schedule needs specialist escalation.
tasks.altitude: Operating authority and schedule responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate operating commitments with technical specialists
reach.learn: Network obligations and plant authority boundaries

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: voltage-schedule judgement remains human here; existing automatic regulation is not newly removed manager effort.

assumptions: Boundary is manager voltage-schedule decisions and coordination, excluding controller runtime and technical engineering studies.

OTHER means plant process-control system. The network authority supplies requirements and existing instruments provide readings; the manager checks applicability and operating limits during s1. No free structured safe-schedule flag is assumed.
Test existing native displays first. Zero incremental upkeep because no new control or decision software is proposed.
unknowns: Network obligations, plant limits and delegated authority
research_questions: Which schedule changes require specialist or network approval beyond the manager?

already_counted.description: Schedule assessment, approval and operational coordination

approvals.approved_version: Exact schedule decision, station, time period, network requirements and plant-condition snapshot checked in s1; changed conditions void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Schedule judgement and coordination remain; controller runtime is excluded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Plant and document decisions stay human; narrowly bounded procedure drafting offers a small conditional gain.
reach: Coordinate operational evidence and implementation with technical specialists.
role.ambitious_version: Clearer evaluation procedures while retaining plant-specific engineering and operating responsibility.
